{{Short description|British mathematician (1927–2016)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''Geoffrey Colin Shephard''' (16 August 1927 - 3 August 2016)<ref name="MacTutorBio">{{cite web |last=J J O'Connor and E F Robertson |date=2023 |title=Geoffrey Colin Shephard|url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Shephard/ |website=[[MacTutor History of Mathematics Archive]] |access-date=9 October 2024}}</ref> was a British mathematician who worked on convex geometry and reflection groups. He asked [[Shephard's problem]] on the volumes of projected convex bodies, posed [[Shephard's conjecture|another problem]] on polyhedral nets, proved the [[Shephard–Todd theorem]] in invariant theory of finite groups, began the study of [[complex polytope]]s, and classified the [[complex reflection group]]s.

Shephard earned his Ph.D. in 1954 from [[Queens' College, Cambridge]], under the supervision of [[J. A. Todd]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|name=Geoffrey Colin Shephard|id=124232}}</ref> He was a professor of mathematics at the [[University of East Anglia]] until his retirement.<ref>[http://www.uea.ac.uk/mth/mthpeople/retired Retired Faculty] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120402054220/http://www.uea.ac.uk/mth/mthpeople/retired |date=2 April 2012 }}, University of East Anglia School of Mathematics, accessed 2011-10-09.</ref>
